stem.en: Which of the following is NOT regarded as a transition element?

explanation.en: Zn has a completely filled 3d¹⁰ set both as the atom and as Zn²⁺, its only common ion. Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹, so copper counts as a transition metal.

stem.en: The ground-state electronic configuration of chromium (Z = 24) is:

explanation.en: A half-filled 3d⁵ set with 4s¹ is more stable than 3d⁴ 4s², because of exchange energy and symmetry.

stem.en: The general outer electronic configuration of d-block elements is:

explanation.en: The d-block fills the (n−1)d orbitals while ns holds one or two electrons (Pd, 4d¹⁰ 5s⁰, is an exception).

stem.en: The electronic configuration of Cu⁺ (Z of Cu = 29) is:

explanation.en: Cu is [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹. Ions lose the 4s electron first, so Cu⁺ is [Ar] 3d¹⁰ (and Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹).

solution.en: Ions lose the 4s electron first, so Cu⁺ is [Ar] 3d¹⁰ (and Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹).

stem.en: Which pair of ions has the same number of 3d electrons?

explanation.en: Mn²⁺ (25 − 2 = 23 e⁻) and Fe³⁺ (26 − 3 = 23 e⁻) are both [Ar] 3d⁵. Fe²⁺ is 3d⁶, Cr³⁺ 3d³, Cu²⁺ 3d⁹, Ni²⁺ 3d⁸.

stem.en: Because of the lanthanoid contraction:

options.en: Zr is much larger than Hf
Zr and Hf have almost the same atomic radius
the 5d metals are much larger than the 4d metals
the 3d and 4d metals have the same radius

explanation.en: The 14 lanthanoids, with their poorly shielding 4f electrons, come before Hf, cancelling the normal increase in size. Zr (160 pm) and Hf (159 pm) are almost equal.

stem.en: Transition metals have high melting points mainly because:

options.en: (n−1)d as well as ns electrons take part in metallic bonding

explanation.en: Many unpaired d electrons add to the metallic bonding, giving high enthalpies of atomisation and high melting points.

stem.en: Which of these 3d metals has the highest third ionisation enthalpy?

explanation.en: Removing a third electron from Mn²⁺ breaks the stable half-filled 3d⁵ set, so Mn has a very high third ionisation enthalpy (about 3248 kJ mol⁻¹).

stem.en: Which 3d metal has the lowest melting point?

explanation.en: Zn (3d¹⁰ 4s²) has no unpaired d electrons for metallic bonding, so its melting point (about 420 °C) is the lowest in the 3d series.

solution.en: Zn (3d¹⁰ 4s²) has no unpaired d electrons for metallic bonding, so its melting point (about 420 °C) is the lowest in the 3d series.

stem.en: Among Cu, Zn, Ni and Fe, the highest second ionisation enthalpy is shown by:

explanation.en: Cu⁺ is 3d¹⁰. Removing an electron from this stable full d set needs a lot of energy (about 1958 kJ mol⁻¹).

stem.en: The highest oxidation state shown by manganese is:

explanation.en: Mn (3d⁵ 4s²) can use all seven outer electrons: +7 in MnO₄⁻ and Mn₂O₇.

stem.en: The only 3d metal with a positive E°(M²⁺/M) value is:

explanation.en: E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V. The high enthalpy of atomisation and ionisation of Cu is not balanced by the hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺, so Cu does not liberate H₂ from dilute acids.

stem.en: Cr²⁺ is a strong reducing agent while Mn³⁺ is a strong oxidising agent, although both are d⁴. This is because:

options.en: Cr is more electronegative than Mn
Cr²⁺ → Cr³⁺ gives stable d³ (t₂g³), and Mn³⁺ → Mn²⁺ gives stable half-filled d⁵

explanation.en: Each ion moves to its more stable configuration: Cr³⁺ (d³, half-filled t₂g level) and Mn²⁺ (d⁵).

stem.en: The oxidation state of chromium in CrO₅ (which has two peroxide groups) is:

explanation.en: CrO₅ has one oxide oxygen (−2) and two O₂²⁻ groups (four O at −1). x − 2 − 4 = 0, so x = +6.

solution.en: CrO₅ has one oxide oxygen (−2) and two O₂²⁻ groups (four O at −1). x − 2 − 4 = 0, so x = +6.

stem.en: Which 3d metal shows only the +3 oxidation state in its compounds?

explanation.en: Sc (3d¹ 4s²) loses all three outer electrons to give the noble-gas Sc³⁺; it shows no other common oxidation state.

stem.en: The spin-only magnetic moment of Mn²⁺ (Z of Mn = 25) is:

explanation.en: Mn²⁺ is 3d⁵ with 5 unpaired electrons: μ = √(5 × 7) = √35 = 5.92 BM.

stem.en: Which of the following ions is colourless in aqueous solution?

explanation.en: Sc³⁺ is 3d⁰: there is no d electron for a d–d transition. Ti³⁺ (d¹), Cu²⁺ (d⁹) and Fe³⁺ (d⁵) are coloured.

stem.en: The catalyst used in the Contact process for making sulphuric acid is:

explanation.en: V₂O₅ catalyses 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃. Iron is used in the Haber process and nickel in hydrogenation of oils.

stem.en: An ion of a 3d metal has a spin-only magnetic moment of 2.84 BM. The ion is:

explanation.en: μ = √(n(n+2)) = 2.84 gives n = 2. Ni²⁺ is 3d⁸ with 2 unpaired electrons. Cr³⁺ has 3, Mn²⁺ 5 and Cu²⁺ 1.

stem.en: Which statement about interstitial compounds of transition metals (such as TiC, Mn₄N, Fe₃H) is NOT correct?

options.en: They are much more reactive than the pure metals

explanation.en: Small atoms such as H, C and N trapped in the metal lattice make the compounds harder and higher melting, still conducting, and chemically inert.

stem.en: When acid is added to a solution of potassium chromate, the colour changes from:

explanation.en: 2CrO₄²⁻ (yellow) + 2H⁺ ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻ (orange) + H₂O. Adding alkali reverses the change.

stem.en: In acidic medium, the number of electrons gained by one MnO₄⁻ ion is:

explanation.en: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O: Mn goes from +7 to +2.

stem.en: In neutral or faintly alkaline solution, permanganate is reduced to:

explanation.en: MnO₄⁻ + 2H₂O + 3e⁻ → MnO₂ + 4OH⁻ (Mn +7 → +4).

stem.en: The number of moles of KMnO₄ needed to oxidise one mole of FeSO₄ in acidic medium is:

explanation.en: MnO₄⁻ + 5Fe²⁺ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O. One MnO₄⁻ oxidises five Fe²⁺, so 1 mol Fe²⁺ needs 1/5 = 0.2 mol KMnO₄.

solution.en: One MnO₄⁻ oxidises five Fe²⁺, so 1 mol Fe²⁺ needs 1/5 = 0.2 mol KMnO₄.

stem.en: In acidic medium, one mole of K₂Cr₂O₇ oxidises how many moles of Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺?

explanation.en: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O. Each Fe²⁺ gives one electron, so 6 mol Fe²⁺ are oxidised.

stem.en: The lanthanoid contraction is due to:

options.en: the increase in the number of shells
the imperfect shielding of one 4f electron by another
the decrease in nuclear charge across the series

explanation.en: Each added 4f electron shields the others poorly, so the effective nuclear charge rises steadily and the size falls from La³⁺ to Lu³⁺.

stem.en: The most common oxidation state of the lanthanoids is:

explanation.en: All lanthanoids form Ln³⁺. A few also show +2 (Eu, Yb) or +4 (Ce) when that gives an f⁰, f⁷ or f¹⁴ configuration.

stem.en: Which hydroxide is the least basic?

explanation.en: As the Ln³⁺ ion becomes smaller across the series, the M–OH bond becomes more covalent and the basic character decreases: La(OH)₃ most basic, Lu(OH)₃ least.

stem.en: Which of the following lanthanoid ions is a good oxidising agent in aqueous solution?

explanation.en: Ce⁴⁺ (4f⁰) readily changes to the common +3 state, so it is an oxidant (E°(Ce⁴⁺/Ce³⁺) = +1.74 V). Eu²⁺ and Yb²⁺ change to +3 by losing electrons, so they are reducing agents.

solution.en: Ce⁴⁺ (4f⁰) readily changes to the common +3 state, so it is an oxidant (E°(Ce⁴⁺/Ce³⁺) = +1.74 V).
Eu²⁺ and Yb²⁺ change to +3 by losing electrons, so they are reducing agents.

stem.en: The spin-only magnetic moment of Gd³⁺ (Z of Gd = 64) is about:

explanation.en: Gd is [Xe] 4f⁷ 5d¹ 6s²; Gd³⁺ is 4f⁷ with 7 unpaired electrons. μ = √(7 × 9) = √63 ≈ 7.94 BM.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The E° value of the Mn³⁺/Mn²⁺ couple is much more positive than that of Cr³⁺/Cr²⁺ or Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺.
Reason (R): Mn²⁺ has a particularly stable half-filled 3d⁵ configuration.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Because Mn²⁺ (3d⁵) is especially stable, Mn³⁺ is readily reduced to Mn²⁺, giving a large positive E° (+1.57 V). R explains A.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Cu⁺ is unstable in aqueous solution and disproportionates into Cu²⁺ and Cu.
Reason (R): Cu⁺ has a completely filled 3d¹⁰ configuration.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true, but the instability of Cu⁺(aq) is due to the much larger hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺, which more than compensates its second ionisation enthalpy. The d¹⁰ configuration does not explain it.

passage.en: To find the strength of an iron(II) solution, a student titrates 20.0 mL of acidified ferrous ammonium sulphate solution with 0.020 M KMnO₄. The purple colour of permanganate disappears as each drop is added, until at 25.0 mL a faint pink colour persists. The student adds no separate indicator.

stem.en: What is the molarity of Fe²⁺ in the solution?

passage.en: To find the strength of an iron(II) solution, a student titrates 20.0 mL of acidified ferrous ammonium sulphate solution with 0.020 M KMnO₄. The purple colour of permanganate disappears as each drop is added, until at 25.0 mL a faint pink colour persists. The student adds no separate indicator.

stem.en: Why does the student not need a separate indicator?

options.en: Fe³⁺ formed is deep red and marks the end point
MnO₄⁻ is intensely purple while its product Mn²⁺ is almost colourless, so the first excess drop shows pink
Acid changes colour when Fe²⁺ is used up
KMnO₄ is colourless in acid medium and turns pink in neutral medium

explanation.en: KMnO₄ acts as a self-indicator: while Fe²⁺ remains, purple MnO₄⁻ is reduced to nearly colourless Mn²⁺; one excess drop gives a persistent pink colour.

stem.en: Which of the following ions have a spin-only magnetic moment of about 5.92 BM? One or more options may be correct.

explanation.en: 5.92 BM = √(5 × 7), i.e. five unpaired electrons (d⁵). Mn²⁺ (3d⁵) and Fe³⁺ (3d⁵) have five; Fe²⁺ (3d⁶) has four (4.90 BM) and Cr³⁺ (3d³) has three (3.87 BM).

stem.en: Which statements about potassium permanganate are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.en: In acidic medium MnO₄⁻ accepts five electrons per ion
MnO₄⁻ is paramagnetic because of unpaired d electrons
In neutral or faintly alkaline solution MnO₄⁻ is reduced to MnO₂
The intense purple colour is due to charge transfer, not d–d transitions

explanation.en: Acid: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O. Neutral/faintly alkaline: MnO₄⁻ + 2H₂O + 3e⁻ → MnO₂ + 4OH⁻. Mn(VII) is d⁰, so MnO₄⁻ is diamagnetic and has no d–d transitions; its colour comes from ligand-to-metal charge transfer.

stem.en: Calculate the spin-only magnetic moment of Co²⁺ (Z = 27) in a high-spin state, in BM, to two decimal places.

explanation.en: Co²⁺ is 3d⁷: three unpaired electrons (high spin). μ = √(3 × 5) = √15 = 3.87 BM.

stem.en: What volume (in mL, nearest integer) of 0.025 M KMnO₄ is needed to oxidise 25.0 mL of 0.10 M FeSO₄ in acidic solution?
Which of the following is NOT regarded as a transition element?

explanation.en: A transition element has an incompletely filled d subshell in the atom or in a common ion. Zn is 3d¹⁰ both as the atom and as Zn²⁺; Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹ and Sc is 3d¹.

solution.en: A transition element has an incompletely filled d subshell in the atom or in a common ion.
Zn is 3d¹⁰ both as the atom and as Zn²⁺; Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹ and Sc is 3d¹.

stem.en: The almost identical atomic radii of Zr (160 pm) and Hf (159 pm) are a result of:

explanation.en: Between Zr (4d) and Hf (5d) come the fourteen lanthanoids. Poor shielding by 4f electrons shrinks the atoms, cancelling the size increase expected for the next shell.

solution.en: Between Zr (4d) and Hf (5d) come the fourteen lanthanoids.
Poor shielding by 4f electrons shrinks the atoms, cancelling the size increase expected for the next shell.

stem.en: Given E°(M³⁺/M²⁺): Cr −0.41 V, Mn +1.57 V, Fe +0.77 V, Co +1.97 V. Which M²⁺ ion is the strongest reducing agent?

explanation.en: The most negative E°(M³⁺/M²⁺) means M²⁺ is most easily oxidised to M³⁺. Cr²⁺ (−0.41 V) → Cr³⁺ (stable t₂g³) is the strongest reducing agent.

stem.en: A transition element is one that has an incompletely filled d sub-shell in its atom or in any of its common oxidation states. By this definition, which of the following is NOT a transition element?

explanation.en: Zn is $3d^{10}4s^2$ and its only common ion Zn²⁺ is $3d^{10}$, so the d sub-shell is never incomplete. Sc³⁺ is d⁰ but the Sc atom is $3d^1$; Cu²⁺ is $3d^9$; Ag forms Ag²⁺ ($4d^9$, e.g. in AgF₂). So Sc, Cu and Ag all qualify.

stem.en: The highest oxidation state shown by manganese (Z = 25) in its compounds is:

explanation.en: Mn has seven electrons beyond the argon core ($3d^5\,4s^2$). Using all of them gives +7, as in KMnO₄ and Mn₂O₇. +6 occurs in manganate (K₂MnO₄) and +4 in MnO₂, but these are not the highest. +8 would need a core electron (it is seen for Os and Ru, not Mn).

stem.en: The most common and characteristic oxidation state of the lanthanoids is:

explanation.en: All lanthanoids show +3 (loss of the two 6s electrons and one 5d/4f electron). +2 (Eu, Yb, Sm) and +4 (Ce, Tb, Pr) appear only for a few elements, mostly where an f⁰, f⁷ or f¹⁴ configuration results.

stem.en: Because of the lanthanoid contraction, which pair of elements has almost identical atomic radii?

explanation.en: Between Zr (4d) and Hf (5d) the fourteen 4f electrons are added. They shield poorly, so the expected size increase from 4d to 5d is cancelled: Zr ≈ 160 pm, Hf ≈ 159 pm. Ti→Zr, Sc→Y and Cr→Mo are 3d→4d steps with no f-filling in between, so the radius clearly increases.

stem.en: Interstitial compounds such as TiC, Mn₄N and Fe₃H are formed when small atoms occupy voids in a metal lattice. Which statement about them is NOT correct?

explanation.en: Small atoms (H, B, C, N) trapped in the voids lock the metal layers in place, so interstitial compounds are harder and more brittle, not softer. They do have high melting points, are very hard (some borides approach diamond), keep metallic conductivity and are chemically fairly inert.

options.en: Their melting points are higher than those of the pure metals
They are softer and more ductile than the parent metals

stem.en: Which pairing of industrial process and catalyst is INCORRECT?

explanation.en: Vegetable oils are hydrogenated over finely divided nickel, not V₂O₅. The other three pairings are correct: V₂O₅ in the contact process, iron (promoted by Mo/K₂O, Al₂O₃) in the Haber process and TiCl₄ with a trialkylaluminium in Ziegler–Natta polymerisation.

options.en: Ziegler–Natta polymerisation of ethene: TiCl₄ with Al(CH₃)₃

stem.en: Mischmetal (about 95% lanthanoid metals, 5% iron and traces of S, C, Ca, Al) is mainly used in:

explanation.en: Mischmetal sparks when struck, so it is used in lighter flints; alloyed with magnesium it is used in bullets, shells and tracer ammunition. Galvanising uses zinc, wiring uses copper and stainless steel is Fe–Cr–Ni.

options.en: Making lighter flints and Mg-based alloys for bullets and shells

stem.en: How many unpaired electrons are present in the Fe³⁺ ion (Fe, Z = 26)?

explanation.en: Fe is [Ar] $3d^6 4s^2$. Removing the two 4s electrons and one 3d electron gives Fe³⁺ = [Ar] $3d^5$. By Hund's rule the five d electrons occupy the five d orbitals singly, so there are 5 unpaired electrons.

stem.en: Calculate the spin-only magnetic moment of Mn²⁺ (Z = 25) in Bohr magnetons (BM). Give the answer to two decimal places. (in BM)

explanation.en: Mn²⁺ is $3d^5$ with $n = 5$ unpaired electrons. $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{5 \times 7} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$ BM.

stem.en: When dilute acid is added to a yellow solution of potassium chromate, the solution turns orange. This is because:

explanation.en: $2\text{CrO}_4^{2-} + 2\text{H}^+ \rightleftharpoons \text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. This is an acid–base (condensation) equilibrium, not a redox change: Cr is +6 in both ions. Adding alkali reverses it. Cr³⁺ is green, and +7 does not exist for Cr.

options.en: Chromate is converted to dichromate; Cr stays in the +6 state

stem.en: Among the 3d series, which metal has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation (and the lowest melting point)?

explanation.en: Metallic bonding in transition metals is strengthened by unpaired d electrons. Zn ($3d^{10}4s^2$) has no unpaired d electrons, so its metallic bonding is weakest: ΔₐH ≈ 126 kJ mol⁻¹, m.p. 419 °C. Mn is anomalously low compared to its neighbours, but still far above Zn.

stem.en: Which of the following ions is diamagnetic?

explanation.en: Cu⁺ is $3d^{10}$: all electrons are paired, so it is diamagnetic (and its simple salts are colourless). Cu²⁺ is d⁹ (1 unpaired), Fe²⁺ is d⁶ (4 unpaired) and Ni²⁺ is d⁸ (2 unpaired).

stem.en: The intense purple colour of KMnO₄ is due to:

explanation.en: Mn in MnO₄⁻ is +7, i.e. $3d^0$: there are no d electrons, so no d–d transition and no unpaired electrons. The colour arises from charge transfer, in which an electron moves from an oxygen-based orbital to an empty Mn d orbital (LMCT). MLCT would need electrons on the metal, which Mn(VII) does not have.

options.en: d–d transitions of the Mn(VII) ion
The presence of unpaired electrons on Mn

stem.en: Copper is the only 3d metal with a positive $E^\circ(\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M})$ (+0.34 V). The best explanation is that:

explanation.en: To form Cu²⁺(aq) from Cu(s) you pay ΔₐH + IE₁ + IE₂, and you get back ΔhydH. For Cu the cost is high (strong metallic bonding and a high IE₂) and the hydration enthalpy does not cover it, so the overall change is unfavourable and E° is positive. The d⁹ configuration alone explains nothing, and Cu does not have the lowest IE₁ or the most negative ΔhydH (Ni²⁺ does).

options.en: Cu²⁺ has the most negative hydration enthalpy in the series
Cu has the lowest first ionisation enthalpy in the series
The high enthalpy of atomisation plus ionisation of Cu is not balanced by the hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺

stem.en: Which of the following is the strongest oxidising agent in aqueous solution?

explanation.en: $E^\circ(\text{Mn}^{3+}/\text{Mn}^{2+}) = +1.57$ V. Mn³⁺ (d⁴) gains an electron to become the very stable half-filled Mn²⁺ (d⁵). For Cr, V and Ti the M³⁺/M²⁺ potentials are negative (−0.41, −0.26, −0.37 V), so their M³⁺ ions are not good oxidants; Cr³⁺ (t₂g³) is especially stable.

stem.en: Assertion (A): Zinc salts are white. Reason (R): Zn²⁺ has a completely filled 3d sub-shell.

explanation.en: Zn²⁺ is $3d^{10}$. A d–d transition needs a vacancy in the d set, and there is none, so no visible light is absorbed and the salts are white. R is true and is exactly why A holds.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en: Statement I: Cr²⁺ is a reducing agent. Statement II: Mn³⁺ is an oxidising agent, although both Cr²⁺ and Mn³⁺ have a d⁴ configuration.

explanation.en: Cr²⁺ (d⁴) loses an electron to become Cr³⁺ (d³, half-filled t₂g, very stable), so it is a reducing agent ($E^\circ_{\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr}^{2+}} = -0.41$ V). Mn³⁺ (d⁴) gains an electron to become Mn²⁺ (d⁵, half-filled d), so it is an oxidising agent (+1.57 V). Both statements are correct.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

stem.en: In a neutral or faintly alkaline medium, KMnO₄ oxidises iodide ions to:

explanation.en: In neutral / faintly alkaline solution: $2\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{I}^- \rightarrow 2\text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{OH}^- + \text{IO}_3^-$. Permanganate (→ MnO₂, a 3-electron change) oxidises I⁻ all the way to iodate. In acidic medium, by contrast, iodide is oxidised to I₂.

stem.en: Green potassium manganate disproportionates in neutral or acidic solution. The mole ratio of MnO₄⁻ to MnO₂ formed is:

explanation.en: $3\text{MnO}_4^{2-} + 4\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Two Mn(VI) each lose 1 e⁻ (→ +7) and one Mn(VI) gains 2 e⁻ (→ +4), so electrons balance with MnO₄⁻ : MnO₂ = 2 : 1.

stem.en: Sodium chromate is made by fusing chromite ore with sodium carbonate in air: $a\,\text{FeCr}_2\text{O}_4 + 8\,\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + b\,\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 8\,\text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4 + c\,\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 + 8\,\text{CO}_2$. What is the value of $b$?

explanation.en: Cr: 8 Na₂CrO₄ needs 8 Cr, so $a = 4$ FeCr₂O₄. Fe: 4 Fe gives $c = 2$ Fe₂O₃. Oxygen on the right: $8(4) + 2(3) + 8(2) = 32 + 6 + 16 = 54$. On the left: $4(4) + 8(3) + 2b = 40 + 2b$. So $2b = 14$, $b = 7$.

stem.en: Which ion has a spin-only magnetic moment of 3.87 BM?

explanation.en: $\sqrt{n(n+2)} = 3.87$ gives $n = 3$ ($\sqrt{15}$). Cr³⁺ is d³ with 3 unpaired electrons. Ti³⁺ (d¹) gives 1.73 BM, Fe²⁺ (d⁶, 4 unpaired) 4.90 BM and Ni²⁺ (d⁸, 2 unpaired) 2.83 BM.

stem.en: Match the aqua ion with its colour. Column I: (a) Ti³⁺ (b) V⁴⁺ (c) Mn²⁺ (d) Ni²⁺. Column II: (i) green (ii) pale pink (iii) purple (iv) blue.

explanation.en: Ti³⁺ (d¹) is purple, V⁴⁺ (VO²⁺, d¹) is blue, Mn²⁺ (d⁵, spin-forbidden transitions, so very weak) is pale pink and Ni²⁺ (d⁸) is green.

stem.en: Which lanthanoid hydroxide is the most basic?

explanation.en: Across the series the M³⁺ radius shrinks (lanthanoid contraction), so the M–OH bond becomes more covalent and the hydroxides become less basic. La³⁺ is the largest, so La(OH)₃ is the most basic and Lu(OH)₃ the least.

stem.en: The ground-state electronic configuration of gadolinium (Z = 64) is:

explanation.en: Gd keeps a half-filled 4f⁷ sub-shell and puts the extra electron in 5d: [Xe] $4f^7 5d^1 6s^2$. [Xe] 4f⁸ 6s² is the pattern of most neighbours (e.g. Tb is 4f⁹ 6s²) but is less stable here. 6p is far higher in energy, and 4f⁸ 5d¹ 6s¹ (also 64 electrons) breaks both the half-filled 4f⁷ and the filled 6s², so it is not the ground state.

stem.en: Which statement about lanthanoid ions is INCORRECT?

explanation.en: Ce⁴⁺ (f⁰) is a strong oxidising agent ($E^\circ_{\text{Ce}^{4+}/\text{Ce}^{3+}} \approx +1.74$ V); it reverts to the common +3 state by gaining an electron, so calling it a reducing agent is wrong. Eu²⁺ and Yb²⁺ are reducing agents because they go to the common +3 state, and Ce⁴⁺ is indeed [Xe].

options.en: Eu²⁺ (4f⁷) is a strong reducing agent
Yb²⁺ (4f¹⁴) tends to change to Yb³⁺
Ce⁴⁺ is a good reducing agent

stem.en: Which oxide of chromium is amphoteric?

explanation.en: For one metal, the lower oxide is basic and the highest is acidic. CrO (+2) is basic, Cr₂O₃ (+3) is amphoteric (dissolves in acids and in alkalis) and CrO₃ (+6) is acidic (it gives chromic acid).

stem.en: Assertion (A): The highest fluoride of manganese is MnF₄, whereas its highest oxide is Mn₂O₇. Reason (R): Oxygen can form multiple bonds with the metal.

explanation.en: In Mn₂O₇ each Mn is bonded to oxygens through Mn=O double bonds (plus one Mn–O–Mn bridge), so a few O atoms can satisfy a +7 metal. Fluorine forms only single bonds, and fitting seven F atoms around Mn is not possible, so the highest fluoride is MnF₄. Oxygen's ability to form multiple bonds is the reason.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en: Cu⁺ disproportionates in aqueous solution ($2\text{Cu}^+ \rightarrow \text{Cu}^{2+} + \text{Cu}$). This happens mainly because:

explanation.en: Cu⁺ (d¹⁰) is stable in the gas phase, but Cu²⁺ is smaller and doubly charged, so its hydration enthalpy is far more negative. In water this outweighs IE₂ and makes Cu²⁺(aq) + Cu(s) favourable. d¹⁰ is not unstable, Cu²⁺ is d⁹ (not half-filled), and Cu has a positive E°, so it is not a strong reductant.

options.en: Cu⁺ has an unstable d¹⁰ configuration
The much more negative hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺ more than compensates for the second ionisation enthalpy of Cu
Cu²⁺ has a half-filled d sub-shell
Cu metal is a strong reducing agent

stem.en: When KI solution is added to a solution of copper(II) sulphate, the products are:

explanation.en: $2\text{Cu}^{2+} + 4\text{I}^- \rightarrow \text{Cu}_2\text{I}_2 + \text{I}_2$. Iodide is a good reducing agent and CuI is very insoluble, so Cu²⁺ is reduced to Cu(I) and I⁻ is oxidised to I₂. CuI₂ does not exist.

stem.en: What mass (in g) of oxalic acid dihydrate, H₂C₂O₄·2H₂O (M = 126 g mol⁻¹), is oxidised by 20.0 mL of 0.0200 M KMnO₄ in acidic solution? Give the answer to three decimal places. (in g)

explanation.en: $2\text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} + 16\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 10\text{CO}_2 + 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Moles of MnO₄⁻ $= 0.0200 \times 0.0200 = 4.00 \times 10^{-4}$. Moles of oxalic acid $= \tfrac52 \times 4.00\times10^{-4} = 1.00 \times 10^{-3}$. Mass $= 1.00\times10^{-3} \times 126 = 0.126$ g. (Using a 1 : 1 ratio gives 0.0504 g, a common slip.)

stem.en: A divalent ion M²⁺ of a 3d metal has a spin-only magnetic moment of 4.90 BM, and the M²⁺ ion has more than five d electrons. The metal M is:

explanation.en: $\sqrt{n(n+2)} = 4.90$ gives $n = 4$. A high-spin d⁴ or d⁶ ion has 4 unpaired electrons. With more than five d electrons it must be d⁶, i.e. Fe²⁺ (Z = 26). Cr²⁺ is d⁴ (also 4.90 BM but fewer than five d electrons), Mn²⁺ is d⁵ (5.92 BM) and Co²⁺ is d⁷ (3.87 BM).

stem.en: How many of the following species are coloured in aqueous solution? Sc³⁺, Ti⁴⁺, V³⁺, Cu⁺, Zn²⁺, Ni²⁺, Fe³⁺, MnO₄⁻

explanation.en: Coloured: V³⁺ (d², green), Ni²⁺ (d⁸, green), Fe³⁺ (d⁵, yellow) and MnO₄⁻ (charge transfer, purple), so 4. Colourless: Sc³⁺ and Ti⁴⁺ (d⁰, no charge-transfer band in the visible region for the aqua ions) and Cu⁺ and Zn²⁺ (d¹⁰).

stem.en: Acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ shaken with H₂O₂ and ether gives a blue colour in the ether layer due to CrO₅. The oxidation state of Cr and the number of peroxide (O–O) linkages in CrO₅ are respectively:

explanation.en: CrO₅ has one Cr=O oxygen and two η²-peroxo (O₂²⁻) groups (a 'butterfly' structure). Oxidation state: $x + (-2) + 2(-2) = 0$, so $x = +6$. Treating all five O as −2 gives the impossible +10; one peroxide gives +8, which Cr cannot reach.

stem.en: Which order of standard electrode potentials $E^\circ(\text{M}^{3+}/\text{M}^{2+})$ is correct?

explanation.en: Values: Co +1.97 V, Mn +1.57 V, Fe +0.77 V, Cr −0.41 V. Co³⁺ (d⁶) is a very strong oxidant in water; Mn³⁺ is strongly oxidising because Mn²⁺ is d⁵; Fe³⁺ is moderate (Fe³⁺ is itself d⁵, which lowers the value); Cr³⁺ (t₂g³) is so stable that Cr²⁺ is a reductant. Students who remember only the 'Mn³⁺ is special' idea pick Mn > Co.

stem.en: Consider the statements about $E^\circ(\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M})$ values in the 3d series. I: The value for Mn is more negative than the trend predicts because Mn²⁺ is d⁵. II: The value for Zn is more negative than the trend predicts because Zn²⁺ is d¹⁰. III: The value for Ni is more negative than expected because Ni²⁺ has the most negative hydration enthalpy. IV: The value for Cu is positive because Cu²⁺ has a half-filled configuration. The correct statements are:

explanation.en: I, II and III are the standard explanations: the stability of Mn²⁺ (d⁵) and Zn²⁺ (d¹⁰), and the large negative ΔhydH of Ni²⁺, make those values more negative. IV is wrong: Cu²⁺ is d⁹, and the positive E° comes from the high ΔₐH + IE₂ of Cu not being balanced by hydration.

stem.en: How many moles of KMnO₄ are needed to completely oxidise 1 mole of ferrous oxalate (FeC₂O₄) in acidic medium? (in mol)

explanation.en: Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ gives 1 e⁻ and C₂O₄²⁻ → 2CO₂ gives 2 e⁻, so 1 mol FeC₂O₄ supplies 3 mol e⁻. In acid, MnO₄⁻ → Mn²⁺ takes 5 e⁻. Moles of KMnO₄ $= 3/5 = 0.6$. Forgetting the Fe²⁺ gives 0.4; forgetting oxalate gives 0.2.

stem.en: How many of the following ions are diamagnetic? La³⁺, Ce⁴⁺, Ce³⁺, Eu²⁺, Gd³⁺, Yb²⁺, Lu³⁺

explanation.en: La³⁺ (4f⁰), Ce⁴⁺ (4f⁰), Yb²⁺ (4f¹⁴) and Lu³⁺ (4f¹⁴) have no unpaired electrons, so 4 are diamagnetic. Ce³⁺ (4f¹), Eu²⁺ (4f⁷) and Gd³⁺ (4f⁷) are paramagnetic.

stem.en: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

explanation.en: MnO₄⁻ is Mn(VII), d⁰: tetrahedral and diamagnetic (A). MnO₄²⁻ is Mn(VI), d¹: green and paramagnetic (B). Its π bonds are p(O)–d(Mn) overlaps (D). In acid MnO₄⁻ → Mn²⁺ is a 5-electron change, so the equivalent mass is M/5; M/3 applies to neutral medium (→ MnO₂), so C is wrong.

options.en: The permanganate ion is tetrahedral and diamagnetic
The manganate ion is green and paramagnetic with one unpaired electron
In acidic medium the equivalent mass of KMnO₄ is one-third of its molar mass
π bonding in MnO₄⁻ involves overlap of oxygen p orbitals with manganese d orbitals

stem.en: Which of the following is/are consequences or causes of the lanthanoid contraction?

explanation.en: 4f electrons shield the nucleus poorly, so the effective nuclear charge rises across the series and the size falls (C). This makes Zr/Hf (and Nb/Ta, Mo/W) nearly the same size (A), and the smaller Ln³⁺ ions form more covalent, less basic hydroxides (B). Because the 5d atoms are no larger but have a much bigger nuclear charge, their ionisation enthalpies are generally higher, not lower, than those of the 4d elements, so D is wrong.

options.en: Zr and Hf have almost the same atomic radius
The basic strength of the hydroxides decreases from La(OH)₃ to Lu(OH)₃
It is caused by the imperfect shielding of one 4f electron by another
The 5d elements have much lower ionisation enthalpies than the 4d elements

stem.en: In which pair(s) do both species have the same spin-only magnetic moment?

explanation.en: Spin-only μ depends only on the number of unpaired electrons. Ti³⁺ (d¹) and Cu²⁺ (d⁹): 1 each. V³⁺ (d²) and Ni²⁺ (d⁸): 2 each. Mn²⁺ and Fe³⁺ (both d⁵): 5 each. Cr³⁺ (d³) has 3 but Fe²⁺ (d⁶, high spin) has 4, so D is not a match.

stem.en: Which of the following statements about the actinoids is/are correct?

explanation.en: Every actinoid is radioactive (A). 5f electrons shield even more poorly than 4f, so the actinoid contraction per element is greater (B). 5f, 6d and 7s are close in energy and 5f orbitals extend further out (D), so actinoids show many oxidation states (up to +7 for Np and Pu): C is false.

options.en: The contraction from element to element is greater in the actinoids than in the lanthanoids
Like the lanthanoids, the actinoids show almost only the +3 oxidation state
5f orbitals are less buried than 4f orbitals, so 5f electrons take part in bonding more readily

stem.en: Which of the following statements about potassium dichromate is/are correct?

explanation.en: A: chromite → Na₂CrO₄ → Na₂Cr₂O₇ → K₂Cr₂O₇ (with KCl); the solid is orange. B: $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 8\text{H}^+ + 3\text{H}_2\text{S} \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 3\text{S} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$. D: acid favours dichromate, alkali favours chromate. C is wrong: $2(+1) + 2x + 7(-2) = 0$ gives $x = +6$.

options.en: It is an orange solid prepared industrially from chromite ore (FeCr₂O₄)
Acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ oxidises H₂S to sulphur
The oxidation state of Cr in K₂Cr₂O₇ is +7
The chromate–dichromate interconversion depends on the pH of the solution

stem.en: Among V, Cr, Mn and Fe, which element has the highest third ionisation enthalpy?

explanation.en: The third electron is removed from the M²⁺ ion. Mn²⁺ is $3d^5$, a half-filled sub-shell, so removing an electron from it costs extra (IE₃ of Mn ≈ 3260 kJ mol⁻¹, against about 2830 for V, 2990 for Cr and 2960 for Fe). Fe has the higher nuclear charge, but removing an electron from Fe²⁺ (d⁶) produces the stable d⁵ Fe³⁺, so its IE₃ is lower.
